definition.title: Complete a commitment
definition.responsibility: Find one complete static operating choice that satisfies every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted joint scenario, then compare feasible choices.
invariants: Choices are finite, input-only controls. One complete assignment is shared across every admitted scenario and obligation.
Admitted joint scenarios are explicit facts; neither independence, probabilities nor unlisted scenarios are inferred.
An empty admitted basis is inconsistent, never a vacuous feasibility result.
Typed acyclic expressions separate static controls, scenario consequences and post-scenario preference aggregates.
Activities, calendars, bookings and permission validity use half-open intervals; adjacent intervals do not overlap.
Capacity is the sum of simultaneous renewable demands. A scoped grant must cover its entire required operation.
Expense sums nonrefundable charges. Refundable holds affect cash only; simultaneous cash events are netted before peak cash is measured.
Every mandatory condition must pass for the same choice in every admitted scenario. Preference cannot compensate for failure.
Ranking is lexicographic over feasible choices only; genuine ties are retained and identifiers only stabilize display order.
A fully checked witness establishes existence during partial search. No-plan and optimality claims require complete relevant coverage.
Missing data, unresolved lookups, unsafe arithmetic and unsupported declarations are invalid input, never invented facts.
Calculated feasibility is conditional on accepted facts and fixed assumptions, not permission, reservation or evidence of actual completion.

expressionLanguage.literals: Finite scalar or homogeneous scalar-array data; no executable code.

operators.add: At least two compatible numbers -> number
operators.mul: Two numbers with at most one dimensional operand -> number; count is a multiplicity
operators.lookup: Complete primary-key binding in a typed input table -> exactly one selected scalar; missing or ambiguous lookup is invalid
operators.exists: Typed equality bindings plus optional row-scoped predicate -> boolean; no match is false
operators.interval-covered: Typed selected calendar rows and a positive half-open interval -> boolean; adjacent coverage may combine
operators.worst-case: Numeric expression -> maximum across admitted scenarios for preference only; nested or unreduced scenario aggregates are invalid

caseDerivation: All case parameters and keyed input rows use the frozen module.inputs types, units, bounds, keys and references; no missing-value defaults or coercion are inferred.
Finite choices draw only from input arrays, input table columns or fixed literal domains; the same assignment applies to every scenario.
The scenarioDomain table explicitly lists admitted joint scenarios; an empty table is an inconsistent basis rather than vacuous feasibility.
Activity graphs, constraints, mandatory obligations, resource mappings, financial mode and preference remain frozen module declarations.
Provenance describes accepted factual sources; identifying a source does not authenticate it or infer readiness.

module.title: Review a street-team deployment
module.question: Which promotion plans meet the recorded staffing, timing, access and spending requirements?
module.description: Compare the listed promotion plans for one venue and event. Show every plan that meets the recorded requirements and let the responsible manager record a choice. Guest targets explain the costs to recover; they do not establish promotion effectiveness.

units.timeOrigin: 00:00 on the recorded operating date; one same-day local clock

assumptions: The starter case contains fictional names, records, event details, quantities and financial amounts. Replace and review these values for the planned activity.
Choose one listed promotion plan before departure. The plans are alternatives; this review does not combine teams, stagger shifts or generate responses to later events.

Every staff member counted can cover the required inside work and remains available throughout the full team absence. Individual stations, breaks, travel staffing and other bookings are outside this review.
Available qualified staff equals the roster count minus unavailable staff. Required inside staffing applies throughout the full absence, not only when the team leaves.

Each plan quote includes its full additional cash expense. Past and already committed costs are excluded. Separate discount loss on existing customers reduces contribution but is not another cash charge for sending the team.

Access and spending records are treated as the complete permission register for this review. Missing, false, expired, unrelated or unsourced records do not establish permission. The manager’s choice and approval of the chosen plan are recorded separately.
All times are local minutes from midnight on one operating date. Event exit and customer travel times are planning inputs; they do not establish attendance or acceptance of an offer.

This review does not forecast additional guests, estimate response probabilities or rank expected profit. Not sending a team remains an available option; its zero expense does not make it the preferred choice.

questions.label: Qualified staffing and operating scope
questions.question: Who remains available inside while the promotion team is away?
questions.meaning: Same venue, event and operating date. Count only staff qualified and available throughout the complete absence; unavailable staff are subtracted once.

questions.label: Promotion timing
questions.question: Can the team reach departing event guests with enough time for them to visit the venue?
questions.meaning: Use local minutes from midnight on the operating date. Customer travel time assumes the guest accepts the offer; it does not predict acceptance.

questions.label: Recorded event access
questions.question: Do current event records permit this activity for the whole contact window?
questions.meaning: Record the venue, event, date, permitted activity, supporting source and valid time period. An empty list does not establish access permission.

questions.label: Promotion expense and spending authority
questions.question: What additional expense and recorded spending authority apply to this promotion?
questions.meaning: USD cents. Each plan quote includes its full additional expense. The spending limit and delegated permission are separate from approval of the chosen plan.

questions.label: Venue contribution per additional guest
questions.question: How much contribution would the venue retain per additional guest under each offer?
questions.meaning: USD cents retained by the venue per additional guest after the offer and variable costs. Additional means a visit caused by the promotion; returning customers can count. A visit attributed to an offer is not necessarily additional. Unknown remains unknown; zero or negative contribution cannot cover a positive cost. Break-even counts cover the plan’s additional expense plus any separate existing-customer discount loss.

questions.label: Separate discount loss on existing customers
questions.question: Would an offer reduce contribution from guests who would have come anyway?
questions.meaning: USD cents of additional contribution lost on guests who would have attended anyway. Include only loss not already counted in guest contribution or the plan’s expense. Break-even counts cover additional expense plus this separate loss. Unknown leaves the guest target unassessed.
